subject: indexation problem with the covariate in preferential sampling

messages.author: ef76f4ec1ca10943
messages.subject: indexation problem with the covariate in preferential sampling
parts:
Hello,

I am working on a dataset under preferential sampling. I have followed the spde tutorial but I am struggling with the indexation of the covariate in the mesh.

In my case, there is an important covariate that drives the spatial distribution of the samples and, apart from the spatial field, I want to correct the effect of this covariate. Unfortunately, I am having trouble with its indexation.

"Covariate does not match 'values' X times. Indexes for mismatch..."

I am afraid that it is related with the fact that I do not completely understand the way in which inla.stack() assigns the indexation of the observation points to the nodes of the mesh. Is there any document where this is explained?

I attach some code based on the spde tutorial that shows my problem.

Thank you very much in advance,
Iosu

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] indexation problem with the covariate in preferential sampling
parts:
On 13/03/16 12:38, Iosu Paradinas wrote:
"Covariate does not match 'values' X times. Indexes for mismatch..."

The problem is not related to the stack functionality instead due to the fact that you did use inla.group() twice and tried to copy one from the other. In order to have it working you do need to do the same discretization/grouping for the covariate. You may do something like:
  covariate.ppy.g <- inla.group(c(covariate.pp, covariate.y))
and them use the first nv + n.c values for the 'pp' stack:
                                        covariate.pp=covariate.ppy.g[1:(nv+n.c)])))
and the last n.v values for the 'y' stack
                                       covariate.y=covariate.ppy.g[nv+1:n.c])))


Elias

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] indexation problem with the covariate in preferential sampling
parts:
Dear INLA users,

After correcting the error noticed by Elias, I thought the code would be ok, but I recently noticed that I was doing something else wrong. I attach an updated simulation based on the latest spde tutorial to reproduce my problem. I pressume the problem is on the observation matrix (inla.spde.make.A()) that I pass to the the inla.stack(). I also add a possible solution to the problem, but I am not very convinced.

I noticed this when changing the side of the scaling parameter in the PS model. So, with my previous code this one runs:
form_covar2 <- y ~ 0 + b0.pp + b0.y +  f(covariate.pp, model="rw1") + f(covariate.y, copy='covariate.pp', fixed=FALSE)
But this one doesn't:
form_covar1 <- y ~ 0 + b0.pp + b0.y +  f(covariate.y, model="rw2") + f(covariate.pp, copy='covariate.y', fixed=FALSE)
"Error in inla(form_covar1, family = c("gaussian", "poisson"), data = inla.stack.data(j.stk), : 
  f(covariate.pp). Covariate does not match 'values' 9 times. Indexes for mismatch:139 141 146 149 150 152 157 158 162. This is not what you want. Use NA values in the covariate!"

As I mentioned, I do also add a possible solution at the very end of the code but I pressume there is still something wrong since fitted effects do differ significantly when I "copy" the pp effect on the marks and viceversa.

I hope this is useful to other people too. Thanks very much,
Iosu

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] indexation problem with the covariate in preferential sampling
parts:
that could be if one of 'covariate.y', 'covariate.pp' is a subset of
the other one. you can define which values/locations the model is
defined on, with values=..., so with

f(covariate.y, model='rw2', values='covariate.pp') + f(...)

should be ok. maybe you need to use unique(sort(covariate.pp)) instead
for values

H
